title: Entropy Additivity for n i.i.d. Copies: H(X^n)=n H(X) by Induction

problemStatement.formal:
H\!\left(p^{\otimes n}\right) = n \cdot H(p),
\qquad
p^{\otimes n}(x_1,\dots,x_n) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} p(x_i),
\quad
\sum_x p(x) = 1.
problemStatement.plain: The parent proof shows that for two *independent* sources the entropies add: $H(p_X \otimes p_Y) = H(p_X) + H(p_Y)$. This problem asks to iterate that fact to $n$ identical, independent copies of one source. A block of $n$ i.i.d. symbols carries exactly $n$ times the information of a single symbol, so its entropy is $n \cdot H(p)$. The claim is a clean induction on $n$: the base case is $H(p^{\otimes 0}) = 0$ (and $H(p^{\otimes 1}) = H(p)$), and the step peels off one factor with the already-proven pairwise additivity.
